finding_key: packages/cli/src/output/formatter.ts::`backenderrorenvelope` discards the server's error message for bodies whose `error` is not an object (e.g. nest's default `{statuscode, message, error: "not found"}`)
evidence: Verified against formatter.ts lines 96–116: `backendErrorEnvelope` only reads `data.error`, and when that is a string (Nest's default `{statusCode, message, error: "Not Found"}` body) the `typeof raw === 'object'` guard makes `fields = {}`, so both code and message fall back to the generic `HTTP_ERROR`/`HTTP <status>` — the top-level `message` is never read. Call sites (e.g. docs.ts `if (body?.error)`) are entered by a truthy string `error`, and the pre-change code at those sites printed the body verbatim, preserving the server's message. So the described loss of diagnostic text is real, though impact is limited to error-message fidelity, not incorrect success-path behavior.
